proofs.proof_tex:
At \(c=c^\dagger\), the definition of the contrast-weighted allocation gives
\[
q^\star=(|1|/2,|-1/4|/2,|-3/4|/2)
=(1/2,1/8,3/8)=q^\dagger.
\tag{1}
\]
The uniform-risk upper theorem therefore supplies a total estimator
\(\delta_n^\star\in[-1,1]\) under the independent design \(q^\dagger\) and a
finite constant \(B_{c^\dagger}\) such that
\[
\max_{y\in\{0,1\}^{n\times3}}
\mathbb E_y\!\left[
\{\delta_n^\star-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2\right]
\le \frac1n-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}n^{-4/3}
+B_{c^\dagger}n^{-3/2}.
\tag{2}
\]

Let \(a_j=-1+j/G\), \(0\le j\le2G\), be the action grid from the evaluator
definition, and put \(\Delta=1/G\).  Fix a realized observation \(\omega\).
If \(d_\omega:=\delta_n^\star(\omega)<1\), choose the unique
\(j\in\{0,\ldots,2G-1\}\) for which
\(a_j\le d_\omega<a_{j+1}\), put
\[
\lambda_\omega=\frac{d_\omega-a_j}{\Delta}\in[0,1),
\tag{3}
\]
and return \(a_{j+1}\) with conditional probability \(\lambda_\omega\) and
\(a_j\) otherwise.  If \(d_\omega=1\), return \(a_{2G}=1\).  Denote the
resulting randomized action by \(A_\omega^{\mathrm{grid}}\).  Equation \((3)\)
gives
\[
\mathbb E[A_\omega^{\mathrm{grid}}\mid\omega]=d_\omega,
\qquad
\operatorname{Var}(A_\omega^{\mathrm{grid}}\mid\omega)
=\lambda_\omega(1-\lambda_\omega)\Delta^2
\le\frac1{4G^2},
\tag{4}
\]
where the variance is zero in the endpoint case.  Thus, for every
\(\tau\in[-1,1]\), conditional square completion yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E\!\left[
\{A_\omega^{\mathrm{grid}}-\tau\}^2\mid\omega\right]
&=\{d_\omega-\tau\}^2
+\operatorname{Var}(A_\omega^{\mathrm{grid}}\mid\omega)\\
&\le\{d_\omega-\tau\}^2+\frac1{4G^2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]
The probabilities in \((3)\) define a feasible Markov kernel for the finite
action-grid linear program; feasibility does not require them to be rational,
because the program is optimized over real decision variables.  Taking
expectations in \((5)\), maximizing over the finite schedule set, and then
using optimality of \(U_n\) and \((2)\), gives
\[
U_n\le \frac1n-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}n^{-4/3}
+B_{c^\dagger}n^{-3/2}+\frac1{4G^2}.
\tag{6}
\]
The independent allocation and the returned grid kernel are an admissible
design--estimator pair in the risk game.  Hence the infimum in that definition
also gives
\[
R_n(c^\dagger)\le U_n.
\tag{7}
\]

It remains to relate \((6)\) to the evaluator's outward error.  Let
\(U_{\Lambda,n}\) be its rational upper endpoint for
\(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\).  The evaluator may refine the Airy interval and the
ordered-algebraic positive-part enclosure to respective widths at most
\(2^{-(n+2)}\), which is stronger than the required width \(2^{-n}\).  Thus it
may choose a rational \(e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\) such that
\[
0\le e_{\mathrm{pr},n}
-\left[n^{4/3}(U_n-n^{-1})+U_{\Lambda,n}\right]_+
\le2^{-(n+2)},
\qquad
0\le U_{\Lambda,n}-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}
\le2^{-(n+2)}.
\tag{8}
\]
Since \(G=\lceil n^{3/4}\rceil\ge n^{3/4}\), equation \((6)\) implies
\[
\begin{aligned}
n^{4/3}(U_n-n^{-1})+U_{\Lambda,n}
&\le B_{c^\dagger}n^{-1/6}
+\frac{n^{4/3}}{4G^2}
+U_{\Lambda,n}-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\\
&\le (B_{c^\dagger}+1/4)n^{-1/6}+2^{-(n+2)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]
The last upper bound is nonnegative.  Combining \((8)\)--\((9)\) therefore
gives
\[
e_{\mathrm{pr},n}
\le (B_{c^\dagger}+1/4)n^{-1/6}+2^{-(n+1)}
\le (B_{c^\dagger}+1/4)n^{-1/6}+2^{-n}.
\tag{10}
\]
Because \(B_{c^\dagger}<\infty\), the right side of \((10)\) tends to zero,
which proves ordinary convergence of \(e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\).  Neither the
uniform-risk upper theorem nor any other declared dependency supplies a
computable numerical upper bound for \(B_{c^\dagger}\).  Consequently
\((10)\) alone does not prove a computable modulus of convergence; the
proposed statement records exactly this limitation.

The exact-primitives proposition gives
\[
\kappa(c^\dagger)=\frac58
\quad\text{and}\quad
\tau_{c^\dagger}(m)
=\frac1n\sum_{t\in\{0,1\}^3}m_t(c^\dagger)^\top t.
\tag{1}
\]
The second identity is exactly the response-count representation of the fixed
finite-population causal contrast \(\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\); it is not a prior
mean or a surrogate target.  By the Airy-benchmark definition and the declared
positivity and finiteness of \(C_A\),
\[
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}
=C_A\kappa(c^\dagger)^{2/3}
=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\in(0,\infty).
\tag{2}
\]

The rest of the argument is conditional on conclusions \({\rm(A)}\)--\({\rm(C)}\)
of the allocation-tube theorem.  Fix \(n\) in the admissible tail supplied by
that theorem.  In particular, its live positivity certificate is
\[
\alpha_n(3T_{k_n}^\dagger+4\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A})\le1.
\tag{3}
\]
The face-robust tangent-score lemma and \((3)\) show that every fiber
\(p_{n,x,h,\zeta}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\) used by the prior is a probability law,
with target-coordinate identity
\[
\mathbb E[\theta_t\mid x,h,\zeta]=\alpha_n x.
\tag{4}
\]
Thus the positivity premise of the face-robust permutation-orbit Bayes lemma is
satisfied.  For every outcome-independent assignment law \(\mathcal D_n\) and
every possibly randomized labeled-data estimator, that lemma yields
\[
\operatorname{BayesRisk}(\mathcal D_n,\widehat\tau)
\ge
\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}\pi(r)
\mathcal B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
\ge B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A},
\tag{5}
\]
where \(\pi\) is the allocation-count law induced by \(\mathcal D_n\).
Every schedule in the prior support is an element of
\(\{0,1\}^{n\times3}\), and its loss is computed against the exact target in
\((1)\).  Hence maximum risk dominates the Bayes risk in \((5)\).  Taking the
infimum over exactly the designs and estimators in the risk-game definition
gives
\[
R_n(c^\dagger)
\ge B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}.
\tag{6}
\]

By the exact Airy-tube Bayes-risk definition and finiteness of
\(\mathcal R_{n,3}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
n^{4/3}\left\{\frac1n-
B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\right\}
&=n^{4/3}\left\{\frac1n-
\min_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}
\mathcal B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)\right\}\\
&=\max_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}
G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r).
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
The sets \(\mathcal L_n\), \(\mathcal X_n\), and \(\mathcal Z_n\) in
conclusion \({\rm(A)}\) are pairwise disjoint and partition
\(\mathcal R_{n,3}\): a count vector either has a zero coordinate or has all
coordinates positive, and in the latter case it either satisfies the local
inequality or its negation.  Applying the corresponding line of
\({\rm(A)}\) to each count vector and using \((7)\) gives
\[
B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}
\ge \frac1n-\{\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-\}n^{-4/3}.
\tag{8}
\]
Equations \((6)\)--\((8)\) prove the first two inequalities in the displayed
chain of the theorem.

Conclusion \({\rm(B)}\) of the allocation-tube theorem supplies the total
finite procedure \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}\) and the bound
\[
\max_{y\in\{0,1\}^{n\times3}}
\mathbb E\!\left[
\{\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2\right]
\le \frac1n-\{\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\}n^{-4/3}.
\tag{9}
\]
Its assignment law is outcome-independent and its estimator is a total
admissible action in the risk game.  Therefore the infimum defining
\(R_n(c^\dagger)\) is no larger than the maximum risk in \((9)\), proving the
last two inequalities in the theorem's chain.

Subtracting those risk bounds from \(n^{-1}\) and multiplying by the positive
number \(n^{4/3}\) yields
\[
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_{\mathrm{pr},n}
\le n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\}
\le \Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-.
\tag{10}
\]
Conclusion \({\rm(C)}\) bounds each of
\(e_{\mathrm{loc},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{shell},n}\),
\(e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\), and \(e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\) by \(E(N)\) whenever
\(n\ge N\).  Equation \((10)\) consequently gives
\[
\left|n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\}
-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\right|\le E(N).
\tag{11}
\]
Since \(E(N)\downarrow0\), equation \((11)\) proves convergence of the scaled
deficit to \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\).  Rearranging that convergence and using
\((2)\) proves the asserted expansion and the strict positivity and finiteness
of its coefficient.

This proof is only the algebraic corollary of the root conclusions
\({\rm(A)}\)--\({\rm(C)}\).  It neither proves those conclusions nor discharges
the open allocation-tube obligation.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Let \(U_n\) be the optimum returned by the rational action-grid program in
\(\mathrm{def:evaluator\text{-}handle}\), with \(G=\lceil n^{3/4}\rceil\),
under the fixed independent allocation \(q^\dagger\).  Then
\[
R_n(c^\dagger)\le U_n
\le \frac1n-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}n^{-4/3}
+B_{c^\dagger}n^{-3/2}+\frac1{4G^2}.
\]
Consequently, the diagonal evaluator's rational primal error may be chosen to
satisfy
\[
e_{\mathrm{pr},n}
\le (B_{c^\dagger}+1/4)n^{-1/6}+2^{-n},
\]
and hence \(e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\to0\).  This is ordinary convergence; the
display does not furnish a computable all-future modulus because
\(B_{c^\dagger}\) is not supplied as computable data.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The risk comparison and the displayed rate bound are valid, but the word `effectively' is stronger than the frozen premises.  The only available remainder constant \(B_{c^\dagger}\) is existential and is not supplied as computable data.  A computable error at each individual input together with ordinary convergence does not in general yield a computable all-future modulus.  The proposed claim removes only that unsupported effectiveness assertion and explicitly records the surviving ordinary convergence.

proposed.statement:
For \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), let \(k_n\), the verified spline record,
\(\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}\), \(e_{\mathrm{loc},n}\),
\(e_{\mathrm{shell},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\),
\(e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\), and \(E\) be the outputs in conclusions
\({\rm(A)}\)--\({\rm(C)}\) of
\(\mathrm{thm:unequal\text{-}three\text{-}arm\text{-}allocation\text{-}tube}\),
and put
\[
e_n^-=
\max\{e_{\mathrm{loc},n},e_{\mathrm{shell},n},e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\}.
\]
For every sufficiently large \(n\), the corrected exact Bayes certificate and
the total finite procedure \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}\) output by that theorem
satisfy
\[
\frac1n-\{\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-\}n^{-4/3}
\le B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}
\le R_n(c^\dagger)
\le \max_{y\in\{0,1\}^{n\times3}}
\mathbb E\!\left[
\{\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2
\right]
\le \frac1n-\{\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\}n^{-4/3}.
\tag{1}
\]
The Bayes inequality in \((1)\) is valid against every outcome-independent,
possibly dependent assignment law and every randomized labeled-data estimator.
For every \(N\) beyond the finite startup of the diagonal and every \(n\ge N\),
\[
\left|n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\}
-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\right|\le E(N),
\qquad E(N)\downarrow0.
\tag{2}
\]
Consequently,
\[
R_n(c^\dagger)=n^{-1}-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}n^{-4/3}
+o(n^{-4/3}),
\qquad
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\in(0,\infty).
\]
proposed.justification: Conditionally on conclusions \({\rm(A)}\)--\({\rm(C)}\) of the live face-robust root, this is their complete algebraic risk-squeeze corollary.
proposed.gap: It inherits the open allocation-tube root and therefore does not establish the unrestricted equality unconditionally.
proposed.consumer: Only after the root bridge closes does it supply the sharp fixed-horizon three-regimen precision benchmark.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The statement is unchanged, but its direct dependency map must use only the live face-robust proof basis required by the orchestrator: the tangent-score identities, exact Airy-tube Bayes risk, permutation-orbit lower bound, and open allocation-tube root, together with exact primitives, the risk game, and the Airy benchmark.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove conclusions \({\rm(A)}\)--\({\rm(C)}\) for the face-robust three-coordinate prior: a target-specific Bayes-risk expansion uniform over the local allocation window, every positive-count exterior allocation, and every zero-count face, together with a computable common tail and a primal all-future certificate that uses no existential constant as input.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen tangent-score identity gives Fisher information for the smooth local mean coordinate, whereas the loss uses the random exact finite-population contrast.  A sharp expansion must retain the covariance between the multinomial target fluctuation and the observed score.  Ordinary vector van Trees or a Cauchy--Schwarz separation produces an error of order \(n^{-7/6}\), which is larger than the required \(n^{-4/3}\) correction.  The exact evaluator terminates separately at each finite input but supplies no theorem controlling its future maxima uniformly over allocation counts.  On the attaining side, the only declared analytic remainder is the existential \(B_{c^\dagger}\), so it cannot be used to construct the computable monotone tail demanded by conclusion \({\rm(C)}\).
open_obligations.attempted: I retained the established common-shift repair and checked its exact eight-type dual pairs, the value \(\kappa(c^\dagger)=5/8\), the inverse of \([v,d^\dagger,\mathbf1]\), and the three proper-face invisible directions.  I then pushed the fixed-parameter ledger through the diagonal definition, the exact orbit evaluator, and the rational action-grid rounding argument.  These steps prove diagonal admissibility, same-input lower and upper certificates, and ordinary convergence of the primal error, but they do not provide the missing exact-target posterior-risk identity, the local/exterior/zero-face inequalities, or any all-future computable modulus.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The closed part of the proposed diagonal can be stated explicitly.  Let
\[
\overline N_s=\max_{1\le j\le s}N(j,2^{-j},2^{-j}),
\qquad
d(n)=\max\{s\le n:\overline N_s\le n\}.
\]
For every fixed \(s\), the face-robust ledger makes \(\overline N_s\) a finite
computable integer.  Hence, whenever
\(n\ge\max\{s,\overline N_s\}\), the defining set for \(d(n)\) contains
\(s\), so \(d(n)\ge s\).  The feasible sets expand with \(n\), and therefore
\[
d(n)\uparrow\infty,
\qquad k_n:=d(n)\uparrow\infty,
\qquad \varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}:=2^{-d(n)}\downarrow0.
\]
For every admissible \(n\), the definition of \(d(n)\) gives
\(n\ge N(k_n,2^{-k_n},2^{-k_n})\).  The first monotone inequality in the
definition of \(N\) then gives the stronger positivity estimate
\[
\alpha_n(3T_{k_n}^\dagger+4\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A})
\le\frac12\le1.
\]
The established fixed-input evaluator and orbit-Bayes lemma consequently
produce, at each such input, exact ordered-algebraic values and rational
enclosures of \(B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\),
exact maxima of \(G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\)
on each of the three finite allocation strata, and the valid all-procedure
inequality
\[
R_n(c^\dagger)
\ge B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}.
\]
The rational-grid argument proved this round also gives a total independent
procedure and a per-input rational error satisfying
\[
e_{\mathrm{pr},n}
\le(B_{c^\dagger}+1/4)n^{-1/6}+2^{-n}\longrightarrow0,
\]
but only with ordinary convergence because \(B_{c^\dagger}\) is existential.
What is not obtained is any of the three uniform inequalities in
\({\rm(A)}\), nor a computable common all-future tail in \({\rm(C)}\).  Thus
finite exact evaluation and the closed tangent identities do not imply the
claimed sharp unrestricted limit.

statement_notes.justification: This remains the unchanged face-robust all-design bridge; the exact tangent experiment, diagonal admissibility, and same-input evaluator are closed, while conclusions \({\rm(A)}\)--\({\rm(C)}\) are not.
statement_notes.gap: The missing step is the target-specific uniform Bayes expansion over local, exterior, and zero-count allocations and a computable all-future tail; the existential fixed-design remainder cannot be used as evaluator data.
statement_notes.consumer: The unrestricted sharp benchmark and cross-sample certificate remain conditional until this root closes.

statement_notes.justification: Randomized rounding to adjacent grid actions transfers the total independent Airy procedure to the finite rational action program with at most \(1/(4G^2)\) additional risk.
statement_notes.gap: The resulting error converges to zero ordinarily, but the declared existential remainder constant does not provide a computable convergence modulus.
statement_notes.consumer: It supplies the finite attaining procedure and per-input primal certificate, but not conclusion \({\rm(C)}\) of the open root.
